correctness.rationale: A square-invertible multiplication matrix forces every algebra isomorphism to be monomial; a monomial permutation on a directed n-cycle is a rotation. The weighted cycle product changes under diagonal scaling by an Nth power and under rotation by squaring, proving the exact orbit classifier and divisor count. The diagonal automorphism kernel has order gcd(N,q−1) and lifted rotation stabilizer index r_d. The power equation for idempotents gives 1 or 1+g points. The final weight makes the cycle product uniform. The independently enumerated finite checks confirm boundary cases n=1, extension fields, and all tested rotations; general proof does not depend on experiments.
